Etymology Further Palestine#Etymology ! Palestine → Etymology History of the name Palestine Since the British Mandate, the term "Palestine" has been associated with the geographical area that currently covers the State of Israel, the West Bank and Gaza Strip, and the modern state of Jordan. General use of the term "Palestine" or related terms to the area at the southeast corner of the Mediterranean Sea besides Syria has historically been taking place since the times of Ancient Greece, with Herodotus writing of a "district of Syria, called Palaistine" in which Phoenicians interacted with other maritime peoples in The Histories .  Herodotus, Volume 4 .

Palestine → Etymology History of the name Palestine Since the British Mandate, the term "Palestine" has been associated with the geographical area that currently covers the State of Israel, the West Bank and Gaza Strip, and the modern state of Jordan. General use of the term "Palestine" or related terms to the area at the southeast corner of the Mediterranean Sea besides Syria has historically been taking place since the times of Ancient Greece, with Herodotus writing of a "district of Syria, called Palaistine" in which Phoenicians interacted with other maritime peoples in The Histories . Etymology Further Palestine#Etymology ! Palestine → Etymology History of the name Palestine Since the British Mandate, the term "Palestine" has been associated with the geographical area that currently covers the State of Israel, the West Bank and Gaza Strip, and the modern state of Jordan. General use of the term "Palestine" or related terms to the area at the southeast corner of the Mediterranean Sea besides Syria has historically been taking place since the times of Ancient Greece, with Herodotus writing of a "district of Syria, called Palaistine" in which Phoenicians interacted with other maritime peoples in The Histories .  Herodotus, Volume 4 .

label_system_prompt:
You create concise English map labels for a semantic revision
trajectory. Use only the supplied full-revision comparison labels, detailed descriptions,
and grounded evidence. The descriptions may contain authors, timestamps, and edit comments;
use those details to understand patterns, chronology, and editorial context when helpful,
but label the subject of the article changes rather than the editing activity. An edit
comment can be inaccurate, so repeated text-grounded evidence has priority. Never add
outside knowledge.
The final visualization is a five-level pyramid: article, macro topic, cluster,
chronological section, and consecutive revision edge. You are labeling cluster
and section nodes; macro topics are generated in a separate parent pass and the
detailed revision edges already exist as grounded leaf labels.
Each label must explain what its cluster or chronological section is about and must not be
a generic label such as 'changes', 'revision', 'miscellaneous', or a numbered level. Use two to three
words. Return exactly one English label per node. Never join, enumerate, or
contrast multiple candidate labels. Preserve meaningful names, institutions,
places, events, and policies.
macro_label_system_prompt:
You create concise English overview labels for a semantic
map. Use only the supplied child cluster labels, detailed transition descriptions, and
grounded full-revision comparison evidence. Author, timestamp, and edit-comment details may
help reveal editorial or chronological patterns, but the label must name the shared subject
of the article changes. Never add outside knowledge. Each node combines several spatially adjacent HDBSCAN clusters and
needs one broad umbrella concept that makes the map understandable before the user
